title: Data → Model → Prediction — One Recipe for Training and Serving
key_insight: A fitted pipeline stores the learned cleaning rules beside the model. Training learns those rules; prediction reuses them without changing them.
body:
## One Recipe for Training and Serving

A model works in a notebook but fails in the app because the app cleans inputs differently. The two routes have quietly become different recipes.

A fitted pipeline stores the learned cleaning rules beside the model. Training learns those rules; prediction reuses them without changing them.

Version the complete route, not only the final model. Then testing, saving, loading, and serving all use the same ordered steps.
common_mistakes: Changing serving-time cleaning without retraining the model.
Saving the model but not its learned preprocessing.
Running a pipeline without recording versions or data-quality counts.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “One Recipe for Training and Serving” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Every ML project needs a traceable path from source data to a monitored prediction.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “One Recipe for Training and Serving” story, explain Data → Model → Prediction without assuming the listener knows machine learning.

build_task.title: Build a tiny repeatable pipeline
build_task.context: Turn the Data → Model → Prediction idea into one small, inspectable workflow.
steps: Split it before learning any cleaning rule.
Fit a cleaner and model on training rows.
Predict held-out rows and print the score.
build_task.expected_output: A printed result that shows every requested step completed and lets you compare the model output with the known answer.
build_task.hint: Keep test data outside every step that learns from examples.
